title: Disability and situational access needs
learningObjectives: Explain disability and situational access needs and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Accessibility considers permanent, temporary, and situational barriers. A user may navigate with a screen reader, keyboard, voice input, switch device, magnification, captions, or reduced motion. Context such as bright sunlight, noisy surroundings, or a broken hand can also affect access.
understand.whyItMatters: Designing for varied needs improves usability for a wider audience and reduces reliance on one input or sensory channel.
understand.analogy: Accessibility is designing several reliable routes to the same destination rather than one narrow doorway.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The list represents examples of access needs, not a complete classification of people.

examples.code: const needs=['Keyboard navigation','Captions','Text resizing','Reduced motion','High contrast'];console.log(needs);
examples.explanation: The list represents examples of access needs, not a complete classification of people.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Review a lesson page and identify barriers for keyboard, screen-reader, low-vision, hearing, and situational users.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.

questions.prompt: What is a situational access need?
options: A temporary barrier caused by the user's environment or context
questions.answer: A temporary barrier caused by the user's environment or context
questions.explanation: Situational barriers can affect anyone depending on context.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable web engineering habit?
options: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
Assume the browser always behaves exactly as expected
questions.answer: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
questions.explanation: Reliable web work combines standards knowledge with real testing and inclusive fallbacks.
